solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Politicians demonstrate case for television commercial breaks

indicators.note: the commercial breaks into the word for demonstrate, splitting it open

parts.note: to demonstrate is to show
AD is short for advertisement, a commercial
an old TV set sat in a wooden cabinet

explanation.surface: Politicians putting on a show, wrapped up in the ad breaks on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposition's team of front-bench spokespeople in the British parliament, a body of politicians waiting to take office.

clue.text: A vegetable? Well no, one certainly not to be pulled up

parts.note: a spring is a natural well of water

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up turns the letters bottom to top, so they read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word no
I is the Roman numeral for one
an emphatic refusal, no

explanation.surface: A puzzled cook decides a vegetable is not the kind you would pull from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: NO, I and NO run upwards to make ONION. The joke is that a spring onion is exactly what does get pulled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A young salad allium with a thin white bulb and green stalk, a common vegetable; the question mark flags the cheeky wordplay.

clue.text: Borders lifted from part of Glasgow for lorry

indicators.note: the outer letters are taken away from the district's name, leaving its inside

parts.note: Partick is a district of Glasgow in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone lifting a lorry across the borders out of a Glasgow district.
explanation.walkthrough: Partick is a district of Glasgow, on the west side of the city. Its first and last letters, P and K, go.
explanation.definitionFit: Artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab and trailer.

clue.text: Players endlessly dart around outside the box

indicators.note: the turned-round dart sits outside, enclosing the box
around means the shortened word is turned the other way
endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a dart is a small arrow
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: Darts players throwing endlessly round and round a box on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' looks like the darts players of the surface, but it means musicians; 'endlessly' and 'around' both work on the dart before it wraps the box.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a band of musicians, and musicians are players.

clue.text: Humbug to swallow while leading a game

indicators.note: the swallowing step comes first, leading the a
the word for humbug takes in the word for while, swallowing it

parts.note: cant is hypocritical talk, humbug
as can mean while, as in 'as I spoke'

explanation.surface: A grumpy player calls humbug and has to swallow it while ahead in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: Nothing in Britain coming up as glitzy stuff

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means the letters read upwards, reversed
nothing sits inside the abbreviation for Britain

parts.note: GB is the abbreviation for Great Britain
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: From nothing, Britain rises into a flashy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming up' works on the whole assembly, so read the combined letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bling is slang for showy jewellery and flashy accessories, things that glitter.

clue.text: Old King Cole united assembly, of course

parts.note: the late singer Nat King Cole, punning on the nursery-rhyme king
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
a rally is a mass assembly of people

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme monarch at a united gathering, as you would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery-rhyme 'Old King Cole' points to the US singer Nat King Cole, who died in 1965, so he gives NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of agreement: naturally and of course each mean obviously, as might be expected.

clue.text: Anything turning up for company?

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reverses the letters

parts.note: owt is Northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: Anything that turns up will do for company?
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is Northern English dialect for 'anything', as in 'owt or nowt'.
explanation.definitionFit: From the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd', a pair counts as company.

clue.text: Marxist, wrong revolutionary?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Is a Marxist a misguided revolutionary?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like part of the definition, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is informal for a Trotskyist, a follower of one strand of Marxism.

clue.text: Belief that leads to imprisonment

definitions.meaning: a firmly held opinion or certainty
a guilty verdict in court that sends someone to jail

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strong belief and the court's finding of guilt that results in prison.

clue.text: Personal item found by whispering burglars?

indicators.note: said softly, the word for burglars comes out the same as the garment

parts.note: nickers are thieves, from British slang nick, to steal

explanation.surface: Thieves quietly discovering something private while burgling a house.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to nick is to steal, so nickers are burglars; the K of the garment is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are underwear, an intimate personal garment.

clue.text: Music genre, a fashion with origin in ghettos

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: A musical style that became fashionable after starting in poor urban districts.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a style of electronic dance music, as in UK garage.

clue.text: Sellers perhaps entertaining a variety of reps, say, in cafe

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the jumble sits inside

parts.note: Peter Sellers was one of the Goons, the British radio comedy team

indicators.note: a variety of signals the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Peter Sellers putting on a variety show for sales reps in a cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers starred in The Goon Show, a 1950s BBC radio comedy, so he is a Goon. 'A variety of' turns REPS SAY into REASYSP.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is a cheap, basic cafe serving fried food.

clue.text: Cheese entices in these mixed meat soups, cheddar finally put in

indicators.note: the final letter is put in among the jumbled letters
mixed signals the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cook stirring cheddar into meat soups at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' turns MEAT SOUPS into MOUSETAPS, and 'put in' places the R of cheddar inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Traps for rodents are traditionally baited with cheese, which lures the mouse in.

clue.text: Rugged coastline of a district

indicators.note: rugged means rough and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugged coastline belonging to a certain region.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectional describes something relating to one section, a part or district rather than the whole.

clue.text: Flight — famous example taking in Italian capital

indicators.note: the famous word takes in the capital letter, holding it

parts.note: a star is a famous person

indicators.note: a capital is a first letter, here of Italian

parts.note: a case is an instance or example

explanation.surface: A celebrated flight of steps that includes a famous one in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a staircase, a run of steps between floors.

clue.text: Song told a story

definitions.meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a German art song and the past tense of fibbing.

clue.text: Forty-five into a hundred is calculated

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A sum: forty-five going into one hundred, worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A forty-five is a single record played at 45 rpm, a vinyl disc.

clue.text: A US writer penning song, not entirely a disaster

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the writer surrounds the shortened song

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song

explanation.surface: An American author writing a song that is something of a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops just the final O of the song before 'penning' puts it inside the writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocalypse is a cataclysmic event, a catastrophe on a huge scale.

clue.text: Essayist after old public house for tragic character

indicators.note: the essayist comes after the other two pieces

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house, used on maps
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A writer leaving an old pub after drinks, for a tragic figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ophelia is the doomed young woman in Shakespeare's Hamlet, who drowns.

clue.text: Vegetable I have to put on tip

indicators.note: the second piece is put on the end of the first

parts.note: the tip of something is its end
I've, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cook with a vegetable placing it on the edge of the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy salad vegetable related to chicory.

clue.text: The novel with very uplifting character

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement
in a down clue uplifting means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: A novel with a character who is very inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' turns THE into ETH; SO turned upward gives OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or nature of a person or community.

clue.text: Far from dangerous handgun initially unable to shoot?

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

parts.note: with no arms, no weapons, you cannot shoot

explanation.surface: A handgun that cannot fire is hardly a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' means weapons, so ARMLESS is without guns; the question mark flags this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmless means safe, posing no threat, the opposite of dangerous.

clue.text: Plant resin under tree? Not me!

indicators.note: in a down clue the resin sits below the tree
the letters m and e are removed

parts.note: the lime is a tree, also called the linden
lac is a resin secreted by insects, used for shellac

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to be the one who puts resin under a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Fur that keeps part of the face cool, did you say?

indicators.note: the question asks how the words sound when spoken

parts.words: keeps part of the face cool
parts.note: something that chills the chin would be a chin chiller

explanation.surface: A fur that keeps your chin cool, did you say? Odd, since fur warms.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech 'chin chiller' ends with the same sound as the animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a South American rodent, prized as fur.

clue.text: Swimmer surrendering head for heart

indicators.note: giving up the head means the first letter is lost

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer giving up a race for the sake of his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' looks like a person but is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The hub is the centre or heart of something, as in the hub of activity.

clue.text: Retired person who's manipulated to get money

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a tool is someone used by others, a puppet

explanation.surface: A retiree who has been conned out of his savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like describing the person, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is slang for money, cash.

clue.text: Artist claims he is able to bend light, by the way

indicators.note: to claim is to take for oneself, so the artist takes in the rearranged letters

parts.note: Francis Bacon, the painter

indicators.note: bend means twist, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist boasts he can bend light, as if in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bend' rearranges HE IS ABLE, and 'claims' puts it inside the painter's name. A Belisha beacon is the flashing amber globe on a pole marking a British zebra crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a light placed beside the road at pedestrian crossings, so a light by the way.
